title: AI and My Values: User Perceptions of LLMs’ Ability to Extract, Embody, and Explain Human Values from Casual Conversations

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-inferred Schwartz values derived from longitudinal user chat logs against users' self-reported baseline surveys to identify systematic model deviations and default priors (e.g., over-estimating 'self-direction' and 'openness to change' while under-estimating 'tradition' and 'power').

Conducting qualitative interviews and blind A/B comparisons of value profiles to observe how the fluency, personalization, and plausibility of AI-generated explanations persuade users to doubt their own self-reported values and over-rely on the system's reasoning.

Qualitative analysis of user feedback to evaluate how the model interprets culturally loaded terms (e.g., mapping 'secure and stable' to specific political connotations) and whether it captures the nuances of diverse multicultural identities versus defaulting to Western-centric norms.
